title: Expired sign-ins and no internet: the pictures

steps.path: A message sent after your Claude sign-in ran out
steps.headline: Claude Code's "Login expired · Please run /login" reply becomes a card with Sign in again.
steps.changed: The reply is drawn as the same red-ringed card the app already uses for ChatGPT and OpenRouter errors, with one plain sentence and the fix as a button.
steps.notice: One press opens the same browser sign-in you used on day one. No terminal, no typing /login. The Settings gear also gets a red dot until you are signed in (your round-two answer); the sample app here already shows one for a sync warning, so it looks the same in both pictures.
steps.risk: Only the most recent expired reply gets the button; older ones in the history become one quiet line: "Your Claude sign-in expired here."

steps.headline: While your browser is open, the card says so and offers Cancel.
steps.changed: New state. No red ring here: nothing is wrong, you are just busy in the browser.
steps.notice: Settings shows the same thing at the same moment, so pressing Sign in again in two places never opens two browser tabs.
steps.risk: Untested on Android: the phone's browser should hand you back to the app when you finish, as first launch does.

steps.headline: Once you are back in, the card offers Continue.
steps.changed: New state. Continue tells Claude to carry on, exactly like typing "continue" yourself, but that word is hidden from the chat (your round-two note); you just see Claude start working again.
steps.notice: The card then reads "Signed in to Claude again" and the conversation picks up where it stopped.
steps.risk: The hidden "continue" is the one part the pictures cannot show; it is built in the next step and you will try it in a dev window.

steps.path: Pressing Sign in again with no internet
steps.headline: With no internet, the browser stays closed and the card turns amber with Try again.
steps.changed: New state. The app checks the connection itself first; only when that check fails does it say "no internet".
steps.notice: You find out in a second, instead of a browser page that never loads.

steps.surface: Chat, on a phone connected to your computer
steps.path: The same expired reply, seen from another device
steps.headline: From a phone connected to your computer, the card says where to sign in, with no button.
steps.changed: Your round-one answer: Claude Code runs on the computer, so the sign-in has to finish there. Same wording as the ChatGPT card already uses.
steps.notice: Nothing opens on a computer you cannot see.
steps.risk: The design guide asks for a button on every error box; this one has none on purpose, by your answer.

steps.headline: The card fits a phone screen, with the button beside the sentence.
steps.changed: The same card at 390 px wide. On the phone app itself the button works (it opens the phone's browser).
steps.notice: Nothing to scroll sideways; the sentence wraps if needed.

steps.path: A message sent after your ChatGPT sign-in ran out
steps.headline: The ChatGPT card gets Sign in again on the card, where Open settings used to be.
steps.changed: Your round-two answer, "match Claude": the fix is on the card, and after signing in it offers Continue like Claude's.
steps.notice: No more hunting through Settings for the right button.

steps.path: A message OpenRouter refused because of your key
steps.headline: OpenRouter's card offers both ways back: Paste a new key, or Sign in with OpenRouter.
steps.changed: Your round-two answer: the app will remember how you connect from now on, and show only that way; connections made before this change see both, once.
steps.notice: Paste a new key opens the same key window as Settings.
steps.risk: Remembering how you connected happens behind the scenes; for anyone who connects after this ships, only their own way is shown.

steps.path: A message sent with no internet
steps.headline: Claude Code's "API Error: Unable to connect…" becomes "No internet connection" with Try again.
steps.changed: Only when the app's own check confirms you are offline; with the internet working, Claude Code's own words stay, so a problem on Anthropic's side is never blamed on your connection.
steps.notice: Try again checks once more and, if you are back online, carries on, like Continue.

steps.path: A message sent with no internet
steps.headline: The same "No internet connection" card in ChatGPT and OpenRouter conversations, straight away.
steps.changed: Today these spend about a minute on "trying again" before "Couldn't reach OpenRouter". With the app's check confirming you are offline, the amber card shows at once.
steps.notice: One card for every kind of conversation.

steps.path: Assistant settings, Cloud providers, Claude Code
steps.headline: The Claude card says when your sign-in ends.
steps.changed: Your round-one answer, "a line in Settings": "Max plan. Sign-in ends Nov 23." Read from Claude Code itself.
steps.notice: Quiet: no dot and nothing in the chat until it actually runs out.
steps.risk: Untested: the date may move later on its own as you use Claude. If it does, the line simply shows the new date.

steps.path: Assistant settings, Cloud providers, Claude Code
steps.headline: An expired Claude sign-in reads "Sign-in expired" with Sign in again inside the card.
steps.changed: Today the card keeps saying "Signed in as…" while every message fails. The notice across the card's foot is the same box OpenRouter's broken key already uses.
steps.notice: Settings and the chat card are one flow: pressing either one updates both.

steps.path: Assistant settings, Cloud providers, Claude Code
steps.headline: A signed-out Claude card gets a Sign in button.
steps.changed: Not asked before, so it needs your yes: today, after first launch, there is no way to sign Claude Code in from the app at all. This reuses the same sign-in.
steps.notice: Someone who skipped Claude at first launch can add it later from Settings.

steps.path: Pressing Sign in again with no internet
steps.headline: Settings' sign-in buttons say "No internet connection" too, instead of opening the browser.
steps.changed: New state. The same check and words as the chat card, for Claude, ChatGPT and OpenRouter.
steps.notice: No more 5 to 10 minute wait for a timeout.

steps.headline: An expired ChatGPT sign-in reads "Sign-in expired" with Sign in again, not "Not signed in".
steps.changed: Today the app quietly deletes a sign-in OpenAI refuses to renew, and the card looks as if you never signed in.
steps.notice: You can tell "it ran out" from "I never set this up".

steps.path: The sign-in page, pressing Log in with no internet
steps.headline: On first launch, a sign-in pressed offline says so under the buttons, and the browser stays closed.
steps.changed: New state. Amber, because it is not a failure; pressing the button again tries again.
steps.notice: A new user without internet learns why in a second, not after a 5-minute timeout.
